title: P99 sampling and cache-warmup scratchpad
body:
Objective:
- Quick exploratory runs to understand why p99 jumps ~4–6x on steady-state traffic vs synthetic ramp. Trying to isolate cache warmup, batching, and grpc connection churn effects.

Hardware / infra:
- Cluster: ded-nyc-prod-pool-3 (4x A100-sXM)
- Deployment: model-instance-v2 (gpt-3.5-ish open model, 16k context, quantized int8)
- Runtime commit: git@github.com:redwood-inference/serving-runtime@a1b2c3d (perf fixes + batch refactor)
- Test harness: local loadgen (python, async), using grpc endpoint with keepalive on/off toggles

Test configs tried (short names):
- steady-50: constant qps 50, 4s gen time avg, concurrency auto-scaling off
- burst-200: 30s burst to 200 qps then fall back to 50
- incr-ramp: 10->200 qps over 5m
- cache-warm: prewarm 1000 prefixes then start
- cold-start: no prewarm, fresh container restart prior to test

Important vars:
- batch_target_size: 8 (default)
- batch_max_latency_ms: 20
- kv_cache_enabled: true (local mem), kv_cache_shards: 1
- connection pool: 16 per client; grpc keepalive: yes/no toggles

Raw run results (key runs):
1) steady-50 (no prewarm) - 2024-11-05
   - p50: 68 ms
   - p95: 220 ms
   - p99: 1.9 s  <-- large tail, often correlated with occasional 10–12s outliers
   notes: CPU on host spikes when tail happens, but GPU util stable.

2) steady-50 (prewarm cache with 1k prefixes) - 2024-11-06
   - p50: 66 ms
   - p95: 210 ms
   - p99: 420 ms  <-- big improvement after prewarm
   notes: suggests KV cache cold misses driving some p99s.

3) burst-200 (no prewarm) - 2024-11-07
   - p50: 74 ms
   - p95: 480 ms
   - p99: 3.6 s
   notes: during burst, CPU scheduler shows many syscalls; observed queuing at runtime dispatcher (batching backlog).

4) increment-ramp (with keepalive off) - 2024-11-09
   - p50: 80 ms
   - p95: 600 ms
   - p99: 4.1 s
   notes: turning keepalive off increased connection churn and p99; suggests rpc-level overhead matters for tail under ramp.

5) steady-50 (kv_cache disabled) - 2024-11-10
   - p50: 70 ms
   - p95: 230 ms
   - p99: 1.8 s
   notes: similar to no-prewarm case, confirms cache helps reduce tail.

6) steady-50 (batch_target_size 16, prewarm) - 2024-11-12
   - p50: 90 ms (increased due to larger batches)
   - p95: 240 ms
   - p99: 480 ms
   notes: batching trade-off: p50 up slightly, p99 similar to batch 8 with prewarm.

Ad-hoc observations / hypotheses:
- KV cache cold misses cause very heavy synchronous work paths (recompute KV, possibly triggering longer memory-bound ops) leading to multi-second p99. Prewarming reduces p99 drastically.
- Connection churn (keepalive off or short TCP lifetime) coincides with increased RPC latencies at tail — investigate client pool sizing and grpc channel reuse.
- Larger batch_target_size raises median latency (expected) but can also absorb variability if traffic spikes are smoothed; it doesn't remove cache-miss-driven multi-second ops.
- Some p99 outliers correlate with host-level background processes (backup/cron). Need to repro on dedicated host with process isolation.

Quick ascii chart (p99 across configs):
- steady-50 (cold):   |********* (1900 ms)
- steady-50 (prewarm): |***      (420 ms)
- burst-200:           |************ (3600 ms)
- incr-ramp no-keep:   |************* (4100 ms)
- batch16 prewarm:     |****     (480 ms)

Debug traces & logs I inspected:
- runtime logs: occasional full-kv-serialization events at time of tail (trace id included in linked artifacts)
- dmesg/host logs: I saw out-of-memory kills on a helper process once (not model process) around 2024-11-07 15:02 UTC
- perf flame: CPU time concentrated in rpc/accept/dispatch stack during tails

Repro steps to run before next sync (fast checklist):
- [ ] Re-run steady-50 on isolated dedicated host with prewarm vs cold, collect perf (cpu, iowait, interrupts)
- [ ] Turn grpc keepalive on vs off matrix with same traffic profile
- [ ] Add a small synthetic tracer in KV path to time cache_load vs compute_miss
- [ ] Run a long steady-50 (2h) to verify if p99 drift or stays stable after extended steady state

Proposed mitigations to test (short):
- Eager prewarm path: on new container start, run lightweight sample of top prefixes from selector service (cheap but reduces misses)
- Async miss handling: if miss path is heavy, consider returning incremental partials or offloading to a helper pool so main dispatch not blocked
- Client pooling guidance: update SDK default to keepalive=true and pool_size >= 8 for sustained QPS

Questions / asks for Jordan/Sanjay:
- Jordan: can you share the KV miss instrumentation branch? I want microsecond-level timers on cache_load and compute_miss.
- Sanjay: any recent infra changes to cron/backup scheduling on ded-nyc-prod-pool-3 around Nov 7?

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- This feels like multiple orthogonal issues (cache miss + client churn + host noise). Best move is to orthogonally test each axis.
- Also consider adding p99 alerting for the route with a "recent-cold-start" tag so we can separate container lifecycle-induced tails from steady-state tails.

Attachments / screenshots (copied links):
- Grafana panel (latency heatmap): https://grafana.internal/d/latency/serving-runtime?panelId=9&from=1699219200000&to=1699305600000
- Perf flame snapshot (s3): s3://redwood-perf/maya/nov07-flame.svg

Next meeting: 2024-11-21 standup if I have reproducible script and perf captures.

End of scratchpad.
